subject: Request: routing quarantine + no-fallback for MedSecure PII workloads
messages:
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: John Smith <john.smith@medsecure.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T09:12:00-07:00
Subject: Request: routing quarantine + no-fallback for MedSecure PII workloads

Team —

Quick summary: MedSecure is asking us to enforce a strict routing policy for a pilot integration handling sensitive PII. They want two constraints enforced for the pilot window (30 days):

- Region lock: all inference must be served from us-west-2 (customer-managed VPC endpoint)
- No-fallback / forced model selection: requests must only go to the approved model variant (redwood-v1-priv-q4_0) — no automatic fallback to cheaper/latency-optimized variants if capacity is constrained.

They made the ask because their data residency and validation rules require consistent model determinism and auditability. The ask came up on the discovery call earlier today (John from MedSecure copied).

What I need from the group:
- Lauren: product guidance — is this policy something we can express with our current routing policies and rollout configs, or does it require a feature change? If it requires an exception path, what are the safety guardrails you want (canary, rate limits, enforced KV cache invalidation)?
- Karthik / Evelyn: security & compliance impact — what additional evidence or controls do we need to provide to MedSecure to sign off (audit log retention, signed attestations, isolation guarantees)?
- Marissa / Ops: feasibility & SLO impact — can Dedicated pools be pinned to only redwood-v1-priv-q4_0 in us-west-2 reliably for a 30-day pilot, and what lead time/commitment is required?

I've attached a simple data-flow diagram from the discovery call and a proposed matrix showing possible enforcement options. John — thanks for raising this, attaching you so we keep transparency while we sort internal trade-offs.

Next step: propose a 30-minute cross-functional sync tomorrow 10:30am PT if that works for everyone.

—Alex
Alex Martinez
Strategic Sales, Redwood Inference
From: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>
To: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: John Smith <john.smith@medsecure.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T10:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: routing quarantine + no-fallback for MedSecure PII workloads

Thanks Alex — good summary. Short answers up front: we can express region lock today via routing policies (region constraint + VPC endpoint) but "no-fallback" semantics are not a single configuration flag currently. We have two viable approaches:

1) Policy-level hard block: update the routing engine to treat redwood-v1-priv-q4_0 as the only allowed variant for that customer_id and return 429 / 503 when capacity is unavailable. Requires a small server-side change and a deployment; estimated 2 sprints (4 weeks) to fully test and roll with canary.

2) Dedicated reservation + strict autoscale: provision Dedicated capacity pinned to that model and set smart routing to prefer that pool; fallback remains possible but can be prevented operationally by disabling fallback routes. This is faster (1 week) but increases cost and requires ops manual guardrails.

For the pilot I lean toward (2) as the path of least resistance if MedSecure accepts a small Dedicated commit. If they insist on programmatic no-fallback (i.e., platform-level guarantee), we'll need the approach in (1).

Guardrails I'd expect: canary at 10% traffic first 24 hours, token-level audit logging enabled, and a rollback policy that automatically reroutes to an internal "safe-hold" endpoint if any error spikes.

Happy to discuss on the sync.

—Lauren
Senior PM, Serving
From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: John Smith <john.smith@medsecure.com>
Date: 2027-04-25T13:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: routing quarantine + no-fallback for MedSecure PII workloads

Appreciate the heads-up. A few compliance notes from my side:

- Audit logs: MedSecure will require immutable request/response logs for the pilot with at least 180 days retention and proof of write-once storage. We can provide signed log digests but need to validate with infra if current retention and immutability meet their bar.
- Key management: requests hitting private models in Dedicated must have encryption keys managed via their KMS or via our customer KMS integration — confirm which they prefer.
- No-fallback implications: if we return 503/429 on capacity issues, MedSecure must accept a risk of unserved requests. If they want guaranteed availability we should recommend Dedicated + burst capacity.

Deliverables I'd like before any pilot kickoff:
1) Proposed SLO / outage playbook (responsibilities, escalation paths)
2) Audit log sample and retention plan (where stored, access controls)
3) Confirmation of KMS approach

We should also evaluate whether requiring determinism from model variant means we need to pin model version exactly (hash/commit) and record that in the action plan.

—Karthik
Security & Compliance Lead
From: Alex Martinez <alex.martinez@redwood.com>
To: Lauren Bishop <lauren_bishop@redwood.com>, Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.com>, Evelyn Hart <evelyn_hart@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: John Smith <john.smith@medsecure.com>
Date: 2027-04-26T15:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: routing quarantine + no-fallback for MedSecure PII workloads

Thanks Lauren & Karthik — that aligns with my read from the call. John (MedSecure) — quick note: if you can confirm willingness for a Dedicated reservation for the 30-day pilot, we can probably stand up the ops route by next week and enable the tight controls Karthik outlined. If you need platform-level no-fallback (so the platform itself blocks fallback routes even if Dedicated is down), we will need more time (product change).

I've scheduled a 30-minute sync for tomorrow 10:30am PT (Ops boardroom / Zoom link in Drive). Agenda: concrete decision on Dedicated commit vs product exception, KMS preference, audit log format, and rollout checklist.

Attachments: MedSecure-data-flow-diagram.png (diagram shared by John), proposed-mup-no-fallback-matrix.xlsx (internal matrix comparing options).

If anyone needs pre-read: see OPS-1428 in Jira and the Drive folder linked above.

—Alex
Strategic Sales, Redwood Inference
